ladder.title: Few edges force property B
ladder.q:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $H$ be an $n$-uniform hypergraph (every edge has exactly $n$ vertices) with fewer than $2^{n-1}$ edges.

Prove that the vertices of $H$ can be coloured red and blue so that no edge is monochromatic. Deduce that $m(n)\ge 2^{n-1}$, where $m(n)$ is the least number of edges of an $n$-uniform hypergraph that is not $2$-colourable.
ladder.source: Alon & Spencer, The Probabilistic Method (Property B chapter); Erdős 1963
ladder.note: The one-line first-moment argument gives the starting lower bound for the property B function $m(n)$.

ladder.title: Turán's construction for the tetrahedron
ladder.q:
Partition a set $V$ of $n$ vertices into three parts $V_0,V_1,V_2$ whose sizes differ by at most $1$. Let $H$ be the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $V$ whose edges are the triples meeting all three parts, together with the triples having two vertices in $V_i$ and one vertex in $V_{i+1}$ (indices mod $3$), for $i=0,1,2$.

(a) Prove that no $4$ vertices of $H$ span all $4$ possible triples, i.e. $H$ contains no $K_4^{(3)}$.

(b) Prove that $H$ has $\left(\frac59+o(1)\right)\binom n3$ edges as $n\to\infty$.

(c) Show by averaging over $4$-sets that every $K_4^{(3)}$-free $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices has at most $\frac34\binom n3$ edges.
ladder.source: P. Keevash, Hypergraph Turán problems, Surveys in Combinatorics 2011 (LMS Lecture Note Ser. 392)
ladder.note: Gives the conjectured extremal example and a trivial upper bound, framing the gap $[5/9,3/4]$ that the rest of the ladder narrows.

ladder.title: Random lower bound for 3-uniform Ramsey numbers
ladder.q:
Let $R_3(n)$ be the least $N$ such that every red/blue colouring of the $3$-element subsets of an $N$-element set contains $n$ points all of whose triples have the same colour.

Prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that $R_3(n)>2^{cn^2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
ladder.source: Graham, Rothschild & Spencer, Ramsey Theory (2nd ed., 1990)
ladder.note: The random colouring gives only $2^{cn^2}$, while the Erdős–Rado upper bound is $2^{2^{Cn}}$; closing this gap for two colours is exactly Erdős Problem 564.

ladder.title: Graphs with no s+1 disjoint edges
ladder.q:
Let $s\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2s+2$. Prove that a graph on $n$ vertices containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges has at most
$$\max\left\{\binom{2s+1}{2},\ \binom n2-\binom{n-s}{2}\right\}$$
edges, and that this bound is attained.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and T. Gallai, On maximal paths and circuits of graphs, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 10 (1959)
ladder.note: This is the $r=2$ case of the Erdős matching problem $f(n;r,k)$: the two extremal families (a clique, or all edges meeting a fixed $s$-set) are exactly the conjectured ones for all $r$.

ladder.title: Complete r-partite r-graphs have Turán density zero
ladder.q:
For $r\ge 2$ and $s\ge 1$ let $K_r(s)$ be the complete $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph with $s$ vertices in each class.

Prove that there is $n_0(r,s)$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ every $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least $n^{\,r-s^{1-r}}$ edges contains a copy of $K_r(s)$. Deduce that an $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ satisfies $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,F)=o(n^r)$ if and only if $F$ is $r$-partite.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On extremal problems of graphs and generalized graphs, Israel J. Math. 2 (1964)
ladder.note: Extends Kővári–Sós–Turán to hypergraphs; Erdős Problem 1158 asks whether the exponent $r-s^{1-r}$ is sharp, and the result also shows $0$ is a jump.

ladder.title: The (6,3) theorem
ladder.q:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices in which no $6$ vertices span $3$ or more edges.

Prove that $H$ has $o(n^2)$ edges as $n\to\infty$.
ladder.source: I. Z. Ruzsa and E. Szemerédi, Triple systems with no six points carrying three triangles, Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 18 (1978)
ladder.note: This is the case $r=3$, $e=3$ of the Brown–Erdős–Sós problem; it settles Erdős Problem 716, and Problem 1178 asks for the analogue for every $e$ and $r$.

ladder.title: Erdős matching conjecture for large n
ladder.q:
Let $k\ge 2$, $s\ge 1$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a family of $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint members.

Prove that if $n\ge (2s+1)k-s$ then
$$|\mathcal F|\le \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k}.$$
ladder.source: P. Frankl, Improved bounds for Erdős' matching conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 120 (2013)
ladder.note: Confirms the conjectured value of $f(n;k,s+1)$ in a linear range of $n$; the conjecture predicts $\max\{\binom{(s+1)k-1}{k},\binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k}\}$ for all $n\ge (s+1)k$.

ladder.title: Improved lower bound for property B
ladder.q:
Let $m(n)$ be the least number of edges of an $n$-uniform hypergraph that is not $2$-colourable.

Prove that
$$m(n)=\Omega\!\left(2^n\sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}}\right).$$
ladder.source: J. Radhakrishnan and A. Srinivasan, Improved bounds and algorithms for hypergraph 2-coloring, Random Structures Algorithms 16 (2000)
ladder.note: Improves the easy $2^{n-1}$ by a factor $\sqrt{n/\log n}$; Erdős's random construction gives $m(n)=O(n^2 2^n)$, and the true order is Problem 901.

ladder.title: Hypergraphs do not jump
ladder.q:
For $r\ge 3$, call $\alpha\in[0,1)$ a jump for $r$ if there is $c>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every integer $m\ge r$ there is $n_0(\varepsilon,m)$ such that every $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n>n_0$ vertices with at least $(\alpha+\varepsilon)\binom nr$ edges contains a subhypergraph on $m$ vertices with at least $(\alpha+c)\binom mr$ edges.

Prove that for every $r\ge 3$ and every integer $l>2r$, the number $1-\frac{1}{l^{\,r-1}}$ is not a jump for $r$.
ladder.source: P. Frankl and V. Rödl, Hypergraphs do not jump, Combinatorica 4 (1984)
ladder.note: Erdős proved every $\alpha\in[0,r!/r^r)$ is a jump; Frankl–Rödl disproved that every $\alpha$ is, leaving open whether $r!/r^r$ itself is a jump (the question behind Problem 1075); Problem 837 asks for the full set of jumps when $r=3$.

ladder.title: Flag-algebra bound for the tetrahedron
ladder.q: Prove that for all sufficiently large $n$, every $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no $K_4^{(3)}$ (four vertices spanning all four triples) has at most $0.5612\binom n3$ edges.
ladder.source: A. A. Razborov, On 3-hypergraphs with forbidden 4-vertex configurations, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 24 (2010)
ladder.note: Razborov's flag-algebra bound $0.5611666$ is the best known upper bound, against Turán's conjectured $5/9\approx 0.5556$.

ladder.title: Mantel's theorem
ladder.q: Prove that a graph on $n$ vertices containing no triangle has at most $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ edges, and determine all graphs attaining this bound.
ladder.source: B. Bollobás, Extremal Graph Theory (1978); Aigner & Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK
ladder.note: This is the base case of Turán's theorem and the first instance of an exact extremal number.

ladder.title: Kővári–Sós–Turán bound
ladder.q:
Let $1\le s\le t$ be integers. Prove that every graph on $n$ vertices with no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{s,t}$ has at most
$$\frac12 (t-1)^{1/s}\, n^{2-1/s}+\frac12 (s-1)\,n$$
edges.
ladder.source: T. Kővári, V. T. Sós and P. Turán, On a problem of K. Zarankiewicz, Colloq. Math. 3 (1954); see Bollobás, Extremal Graph Theory
ladder.note: Gives the upper bound $\mathrm{ex}(n;K_{r,r})=O(n^{2-1/r})$ whose matching lower bound is Erdős Problem 714.

ladder.title: The asymptotics of ex(n, C4)
ladder.q:
Prove that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)=\left(\tfrac12+o(1)\right)n^{3/2}\qquad(n\to\infty).$$

For the lower bound, for a prime power $q$ take as vertices the points of the projective plane over $\mathbb F_q$ and join distinct points $(x_0:x_1:x_2)$ and $(y_0:y_1:y_2)$ when $x_0y_0+x_1y_1+x_2y_2=0$; then use the density of primes to pass to all $n$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, A. Rényi and V. T. Sós, On a problem of graph theory, Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 1 (1966); W. G. Brown, On graphs that do not contain a Thomsen graph, Canad. Math. Bull. 9 (1966)
ladder.note: The first bipartite extremal number known asymptotically; Füredi later found the exact value for $n=q^2+q+1$, which answers Problem 765.

ladder.title: Erdős–Stone–Simonovits
ladder.q:
Let $H$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(H)=r+1\ge 2$. Prove that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H)=\left(1-\frac1r+o(1)\right)\binom n2 .$$

In particular, conclude that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)=o(n^2)$ if and only if $H$ is bipartite.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and A. H. Stone, On the structure of linear graphs, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 52 (1946); P. Erdős and M. Simonovits, A limit theorem in graph theory, Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 1 (1966)
ladder.note: Settles the non-bipartite case to first order, so every remaining question about the order of magnitude of $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)$ concerns bipartite $H$.

ladder.title: A dense K_{3,3}-free graph
ladder.q: Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for all $n\ge 2$ there is a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $c\,n^{5/3}$ edges and no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{3,3}$.
ladder.source: W. G. Brown, On graphs that do not contain a Thomsen graph, Canad. Math. Bull. 9 (1966)
ladder.note: This is the case $r=3$ of Problem 714 (the case $r=2$ is the $C_4$ rung); Brown's construction uses spheres in $\mathbb F_p^3$, and the case $r\ge 4$ is open.

ladder.title: Even cycles: the Bondy–Simonovits bound
ladder.q: Let $k\ge 2$. Prove that there is a constant $C_k$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices with no cycle of length exactly $2k$ has at most $C_k\, n^{1+1/k}$ edges.
ladder.source: J. A. Bondy and M. Simonovits, Cycles of even length in graphs, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 16 (1974)
ladder.note: Gives the upper bound that Problem 572 asks to match from below.

ladder.title: Dense graphs with no 6-cycle
ladder.q: Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ there is a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $c\,n^{4/3}$ edges and no cycle of length $6$.
ladder.source: C. T. Benson, Minimal regular graphs of girths eight and twelve, Canad. J. Math. 18 (1966); R. Wenger, Extremal graphs with no C4's, C6's, or C10's, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 52 (1991)
ladder.note: This is the case $k=3$ of Problem 572, from incidence graphs of generalized quadrangles; the matching lower bound is known only for $k\in\{2,3,5\}$.

ladder.title: Norm graphs
ladder.q:
Let $t\ge 2$ and $s\ge (t-1)!+1$ be integers. Prove that there is $c=c(t,s)>0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;K_{t,s})\ge c\,n^{2-1/t}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.
ladder.source: N. Alon, L. Rónyai and T. Szabó, Norm-graphs: variations and applications, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 76 (1999); earlier J. Kollár, L. Rónyai and T. Szabó, Combinatorica 16 (1996) for s > t!
ladder.note: This settles the order of magnitude for $K_{t,s}$ when $s$ is large compared with $t$; Problem 714 asks for the balanced case $s=t$.

ladder.title: Bipartite graphs with bounded degrees on one side
ladder.q:
Let $r\ge 1$ and let $H$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A,B$ in which every vertex of $A$ has degree at most $r$. Prove that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)=O_H\!\left(n^{2-1/r}\right)$.

Further, prove that if $H$ is bipartite and $r$-degenerate then $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)=O_H\!\left(n^{2-1/(4r)}\right)$.
ladder.source: N. Alon, M. Krivelevich and B. Sudakov, Turán numbers of bipartite graphs and related Ramsey-type questions, Combin. Probab. Comput. 12 (2003)
ladder.note: Dependent random choice proves the Erdős–Simonovits conjecture when the degeneracy bound holds on one side, and gives exponent $2-1/(4r)$ in general, against the conjectured $2-1/r$.

ladder.title: Every rational exponent for families
ladder.q:
Prove that for every rational number $\alpha\in(1,2)$ there is a finite family $\mathcal F_\alpha$ of bipartite graphs with
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal F_\alpha)=\Theta(n^{\alpha}).$$
ladder.source: B. Bukh and D. Conlon, Rational exponents in extremal graph theory, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20 (2018)
ladder.note: This is the family version of Problem 571, which asks for a single graph with each rational exponent; Problem 713(b) asks whether only rational exponents occur.

ladder.title: The Erdős–Szekeres recursion
ladder.q:
Let $R(k,\ell)$ be the least $n$ such that every red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_\ell$.

Prove that $R(k,\ell)\le R(k-1,\ell)+R(k,\ell-1)$ for $k,\ell\ge 2$, and deduce that
$$R(k,\ell)\le\binom{k+\ell-2}{k-1}.$$
Conclude that $R(k,k)<4^k$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and G. Szekeres, A combinatorial problem in geometry, Compositio Math. 2 (1935); Graham, Rothschild & Spencer, Ramsey Theory
ladder.note: Gives the $4^k$ upper bound that stood, up to subexponential factors, until 2023.

ladder.title: Ramsey numbers of a tree versus a clique
ladder.q: Let $T$ be any tree on $n\ge 2$ vertices and let $m\ge 2$. Prove that every red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_N$ with $N=(n-1)(m-1)+1$ contains a red copy of $T$ or a blue $K_m$, and that this is false for $N=(n-1)(m-1)$.
ladder.source: V. Chvátal, Tree-complete graph Ramsey numbers, J. Graph Theory 1 (1977)
ladder.note: An exact off-diagonal Ramsey number by greedy embedding; Problem 551 asks for the same formula $(k-1)(n-1)+1$ with the tree replaced by a cycle $C_k$.

ladder.title: Multicolour triangle Ramsey numbers
ladder.q:
Let $R(3;k)$ be the least $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $k$ colours contains a monochromatic triangle.

Prove that $R(3;k)\le k\,(R(3;k-1)-1)+2$ for $k\ge 2$, and deduce that $R(3;k)\le\lfloor e\cdot k!\rfloor+1$ for all $k\ge 1$.
ladder.source: Graham, Rothschild & Spencer, Ramsey Theory (2nd ed., 1990)
ladder.note: Gives the factorial upper bound; Problem 183 asks about $\lim_k R(3;k)^{1/k}$, and the known lower bounds are only exponential.

ladder.title: Erdős's probabilistic lower bound
ladder.q: Let $R(k)=R(k,k)$. Prove that if $\binom nk 2^{1-\binom k2}<1$ then $R(k)>n$, and deduce that $R(k)>2^{k/2}$ for every $k\ge 3$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, Some remarks on the theory of graphs, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 53 (1947)
ladder.note: This is the lower bound $\sqrt2^{\,k}$, still the best up to lower-order factors; Problem 78 asks for an explicit colouring that does as well as $C^k$.

ladder.title: Local lemma lower bound for R(k)
ladder.q:
Using the Lovász Local Lemma, prove that
$$R(k)\ge (1+o(1))\,\frac{\sqrt2}{e}\,k\,2^{k/2}\qquad(k\to\infty).$$
ladder.source: J. Spencer, Ramsey's theorem—a new lower bound, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 18 (1975); Alon & Spencer, The Probabilistic Method
ladder.note: Doubles the constant from the first-moment bound; Problem 1029 asks whether $R(k)/(k2^{k/2})\to\infty$.

ladder.title: Shearer's bound and R(3,k)
ladder.q:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d>1$. Prove that $G$ has an independent set of size at least
$$n\,\frac{d\log d-d+1}{(d-1)^2}.$$

Deduce that $R(3,k)\le (1+o(1))\dfrac{k^2}{\log k}$ as $k\to\infty$, where $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.
ladder.source: J. B. Shearer, A note on the independence number of triangle-free graphs, Discrete Math. 46 (1983)
ladder.note: Gives the best known upper bound for $R(3,k)$ (Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi had first shown $O(k^2/\log k)$).

ladder.title: The order of magnitude of R(3,k)
ladder.q:
Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(3,k)\ge c\,\frac{k^2}{\log k}$$
for all $k\ge 2$.
ladder.source: J. H. Kim, The Ramsey number R(3,t) has order of magnitude t^2/log t, Random Structures Algorithms 7 (1995)
ladder.note: Together with the previous rung this pins down $R(3,k)=\Theta(k^2/\log k)$; Problem 165 asks for the constant, and Problem 544 asks about the increments $R(3,k+1)-R(3,k)$.

ladder.title: Bounded degree graphs have linear Ramsey numbers
ladder.q: Let $\Delta\ge 1$. Prove that there is a constant $C(\Delta)$ such that every graph $H$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies $R(H)\le C(\Delta)\,n$, where $R(H)$ is the least $N$ such that every red/blue colouring of $E(K_N)$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$.
ladder.source: V. Chvátal, V. Rödl, E. Szemerédi and W. T. Trotter, The Ramsey number of a graph with bounded maximum degree, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 34 (1983)
ladder.note: Bounded maximum degree implies bounded degeneracy, so this is a special case of the Burr–Erdős conjecture (Problem 163), later proved by C. Lee (2017).

ladder.title: The asymptotics of R(4,k)
ladder.q:
Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(4,k)\ge c\,\frac{k^3}{(\log k)^4}$$
for all sufficiently large $k$.
ladder.source: S. Mattheus and J. Verstraete, The asymptotics of r(4,t), Ann. of Math. 199 (2024)
ladder.note: This answers Problem 166 and is the case $s=4$ of Problem 986, matching the Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi upper bound $O(k^3/\log^2 k)$ up to logarithmic factors.

ladder.title: An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey
ladder.q:
Prove that there is an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$R(k)\le (4-\varepsilon)^k$$
for all sufficiently large $k$.
ladder.source: M. Campos, S. Griffiths, R. Morris and J. Sahasrabudhe, An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey, arXiv:2303.09521 (2023)
ladder.note: This is the first exponential improvement on Erdős–Szekeres (later optimised to $3.8^{k+o(k)}$ by Gupta, Ndiaye, Norin and Wei, arXiv:2407.19026); whether $\lim R(k)^{1/k}$ exists and equals $\sqrt2$ or $4-\varepsilon$ is Problem 77.
